title: Your reading
tomorrow: give quietly, or give where people can see? Amira can't decide.

segments.voice: Yesterday, Fatima's three phrases at bedtime: my dhikr, light enough to carry. Today, something with more pages.

A voice note to a friend, deleted and re-recorded four times because one word came out wrong. Reading aloud does that. Now make it a language you're still learning, and make it the Qur'an. Is the stumbling a problem? Here's the odd detail. A hadith doesn't just tolerate the reader who stumbles. It promises that reader two rewards.
screen: `RE-RECORDED FOUR TIMES.` → `A LANGUAGE YOU'RE STILL LEARNING.` → `TWO REWARDS FOR STUMBLING?`

segments.voice: The report is in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said the one who is skilled in the Qur'an will be with the noble, righteous scribes, the angels. And the one who reads it haltingly, finding it hard, has two rewards. Why two? Commentators such as al-Nawawi give a plain reading: one for the reciting, and one for the effort it costs. The stumble isn't held against the reader. It's counted. The Qur'an makes room for limits too. Surah al-Muzzammil opens with a call to stand much of the night in prayer. Its last verse eases that call. God knows, it says, that some of you are sick, some are traveling in search of His bounty, some are fighting in His cause. So recite of it what is easy. That's the solution to the puzzle, and the idea behind a daily portion. Not the whole book in a weekend. A set amount, sized to your actual life, kept every day: a page, a few verses, a short surah. Some read slowly beside an audio reciter; some read a translation alongside. One for tonight: in the hadith, the struggling reader is promised two rewards.
screen: `WITH THE NOBLE SCRIBES.` · `STUMBLING: TWO REWARDS.` · `RECITE WHAT IS EASY.` · `SIZED TO YOUR REAL LIFE.` · then, large: `MY PORTION.`

segments.voice: Open a Qur'an or a translation, on paper or a screen, to any page. Choose one verse and stay with it for the whole sit: read it once, slowly, in whatever language you can, then rest your eyes on the words.
Your reading: a daily Qur'an portion sized to your real life, stumbles and all.
Pocket this: my portion, a page you keep over a book you drop. Four of ten, read.
